mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime. This raises the cost of capital and depresses risk asset valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which reduces earnings growth and drags equity valuations lower over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 1.5% over a 6-month window signals a disinflationary tightening cycle. This combination typically leads to positive equity returns as real interest rates rise but inflation risk abates, boosting risk asset valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (implied by RSAFS growth) above their respective 6-month averages signals robust household demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE dynamics and PAYEMS growth) above its 5-year average, combined with stable unemployment, signals improved labor supply and productivity potential, which supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when labor force participation rises and unemployment is stable for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for more than six consecutive months signals weakness in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials, homebuilding, and related equities, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month MA for more than six months.
